block: SQ3: companion structured review for Essay 2, on instrument choice for agricultural pesticides. Questions: what damage function does the literature assume, and which empirical parameter does it need to rank bans, taxes and buffer zones? Calibration ran 2026-10-11/12, OpenAlex counts are live values from those dates. Recommended OpenAlex design: 8 arms. Three general rules: (i) to keep precision, put the pesticide concept in the TITLE; (ii) cover the off-topic seeds with dedicated arms for nonpoint pollution, prices vs quantities, citation chasing, aerial application and Portuguese/Spanish records; (iii) add Weitzman (1974) by hand as an anchor.

final_strategies.rationale: Searches full text of AJAE, AEPP, Agricultural Economics and Pest Management Science. Retrieved 3 seeds plus the nonpoint instrument-choice literature.

final_strategies.source: Grey literature / web (Parallel web_search plus agency hand-search)
final_strategies.query: site:ageconsearch.umn.edu, site:ideas.repec.org, site:nber.org on pesticide tax/ban/prices vs quantities; buffer zones/setbacks/schools; aerial spraying ban. Hand-search: CDFA-OPCA publications, CDPR rulemaking (DPR 24-001), EPA BEAD buffer impact analyses (regulations.gov EPA-HQ-OPP-2005-0128), EU SUD evaluation (Ramboll 2021, BiPRO 2004), EPRS 2022

seeds_missed.why: Weitzman (1974). Its OpenAlex abstract is only the OUP journal header ('Journal Article Prices vs. Quantities Get access...'), and it is general theory without agrochemical vocabulary. It is handled by hand-inclusion as an anchor and by the citation arm S5 (cites:W1525260320).

known_item_recall.recall_indexed: Primary: 9/9 indexed. Final union retrieves 8/9 (88.9%), and 9/9 with the hand-added anchor. S1 alone retrieves 7/9. Supplementary validation set S-1 (10 items found by OpenAlex title lookups during calibration, so NOT independent of the vocabulary): 10/10. It contains Gunnell 2007, the Danish tax ex post 2023, Norway 2020, the buffer-zone CBA 2009, Finger 2017, Böcker & Finger 2016 (x2), Möhring 2020, EST 2000 and the EU aerial ban 2018. Validation set V2 (12 items found outside the OpenAlex strings, via PubMed index, Scholar Gateway and web): 12/12 across the final union; S1 alone gets 7/12, and S2 (A4), S6, S7 and S8 add the other five.

volume_estimate_after_dedup: OpenAlex counts as of 2026-10-11/12. Core set (S1 1,545 + S2 689 + S3 174 + S4 227 + S5 108 = 2,743 gross; S1∩S2 measured at 30; the other overlaps, among S3/S2-A8b/S5 and S4/S1, were not measured and should be small): about 2,600–2,700 unique. Extended arms add, after measured overlaps with S1: S6 about +570, S7 about +143, S8 +391 at most (overlap with S1 not measured). Total about 3,600–3,800 OpenAlex records. Removing duplicate versions (AgEcon conference vs journal, SSRN vs journal, duplicate DOIs such as Soares & Porto, two records each for 'Spatial heterogeneity and the choice of instruments' 1996/2001 and 'Regulation of nitrogen pollution: taxes versus quotas' 1995) should bring this to roughly 3,300–3,500. The ranked sources add mostly duplicates; grey literature adds about 20–40 agency reports. Trade-off: a title+abstract-only design returns 6,380 and keeps the same 8/9 seeds, but its tail precision is about 0/15. The title-restricted design gets the same recall at less than half the volume. If volume must be cut further, S6 (regulatory cost) is the first candidate to screen with AI prioritization only; it was nonetheless the only arm that found Mace et al.
issues_and_limits: Counts are live OpenAlex values from 2026-10-11/12 and will drift.

Validation set S-1 was located with OpenAlex title searches that use the same vocabulary as the strings ('pesticide tax', etc.), so it overstates recall. V2 (12 items from PubMed index, Scholar Gateway and web) is the more independent test: 7/12 by S1 alone, 12/12 only after adding S6, S7 and S8. Unknown-unknowns certainly remain.

The title restriction (pesticide concept in the title) is the main design choice. It loses papers that mention pesticides only in the abstract, such as general agri-environmental policy and instrument-choice papers. No seed was lost, but the risk cannot be measured beyond the seed sets.

Weitzman (1974) and general instrument-choice theory without agrochemical vocabulary cannot be retrieved topically. S5 covers only citers whose title/abstract has agricultural terms, and it depends on how completely OpenAlex parsed references for a 1974 article.

No Scholar Gateway or research-index result surfaced a Weitzman-style prices-vs-quantities application to pesticides specifically. Such work may be rare, or it may sit in nonpoint/nitrogen papers (S3, S2-A8b) and grey literature.
Overlaps among S3, S4, S5 and S8, and between S8 and S1, were not measured. The volume estimate is a range.

OpenAlex cannot union filters on different fields (title vs title_and_abstract vs cites) in one call. Overlaps were measured by AND-ing filters, and every call echoes the full parsed query (x_query), which makes outputs very long.
Firecrawl's OpenAlex route allows about 12 requests per minute; 1 call returned HTTP 429 and was re-run. The Firecrawl 'query/directQuote' format did not reduce output and costs 5 credits.

No native AgEcon Search, RePEc, SSRN, NBER, EconLit, Scopus or Web of Science search was possible: grey literature was sampled via web search only. EconLit is the main bibliographic gap for agricultural economics. Crossref was not used.

The research index and Scholar Gateway return ranked results without totals. Scholar Gateway payloads lacked titles (DOI, ISSN and snippet only), so some DOIs (e.g., 10.2307/1244419, 10.2307/1243886) were not identified by title from tool output.

Scope issues for the screeners. S2-A4 (HHP bans and suicide) is mostly epidemiology; only studies reporting effects on use/yield/output or cost-effectiveness inform instrument choice. S1-I6 and S7 include farmer health-cost valuation. S4 overlaps SQ1 (health effects of aerial spraying, e.g., Camacho & Mejía).

Agency regulatory-impact analyses (CDFA-OPCA school-site and chlorpyrifos reports, EPA BEAD fumigant buffer analyses, CDPR 1,3-D setbacks, BiPRO 2004, Ramboll 2021 SUD evaluation) are grey literature mostly absent from OpenAlex and need hand-search.
No date or type filters were applied or tested (e.g., excluding paratext/erratum). The seeds span 1974–2024, so no date floor is recommended for SQ3, unlike SQ1 (1990+).
Portuguese/Spanish coverage relies on OpenAlex only (S8). SciELO/LILACS were not searched for SQ3.
S6 was measured with both P+ (738) and P++ (740); the P++ version is the one recommended.
syntax_findings: OpenAlex title_and_abstract.search accepts uppercase AND/OR, parentheses and quoted phrases. 'pesticide' (316,429) AND tax-block (861,056) = 864, and nested OR-of-AND unions run in a single call (6,380).

title.search is parsed as display_name.search. It accepts Boolean expressions, and 2 title.search filters can be AND-ed in one call (S7). title.search plus title_and_abstract.search gives a 'concept in title, other concepts anywhere' design.
There is NO accent folding: title 'agrotóxicos OR agrotóxico' = 3,912 vs 'agrotoxicos' = 79. Accented Portuguese/Spanish forms must be listed explicitly. Stemming is English-only.
Search is stemmed: 'pesticide' matches 'pesticides', and quoted phrases are stemmed ('buffer zone' matches 'buffer-zone'). The bare word 'setback' is generic English and inflates counts (10,266).
cites:W<id> combines with title_and_abstract.search, which gives a reproducible citation-chasing arm (108 citers of Weitzman 1974 with agricultural vocabulary).
Union across different filter fields (title, title_and_abstract, cites, doi) is impossible in one call. Overlaps are measured by AND-ing the filters (e.g., S1∩S2 = 30, S6∩S1 = 170, S7∩S1 = 46).

The doi: filter with pipes is the right tool for known-item recall. A doi containing parentheses (10.1016/s0921-8009(01)00164-1) works unencoded. One DOI can map to 2 OpenAlex records (Soares & Porto 2012: W2000841697, W1916498121).
Relevance-sorted paging (page=N) is a cheap way to sample tail precision before committing to a string.
Some Brazilian articles are stored with Portuguese-only titles (CSP 2020 'Os incentivos fiscais aos agrotóxicos...'), so English-only pesticide blocks miss them.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: The Economics of Pesticide Use and Regulation
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Science overview of US pesticide regulation (bans as the main US device) and its economic trade-offs. Not a seed; retrieved by S1 and S6.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: The Economics of Pesticides and Pest Control
incidental_relevant_studies.why: IRERE review on productivity vs health effects and on policies vs the social optimum; uses the damage-control framing.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Risk-indexed herbicide taxes to reduce ground and surface water pollution: an integrated ecological economics evaluation
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Differentiates taxes by a risk/damage index, so it is directly about which damage parameter a tax should track.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Ex-post evaluation of the Danish pesticide tax: A novel and effective tax design
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Ex post evaluation of the load-based Danish tax: the price instrument in practice.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Revisiting Pesticide Taxation Schemes
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Finger/Möhring line on the design of pesticide taxes in Europe.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: European Pesticide Tax Schemes in Comparison: An Analysis of Experiences and Developments
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Compares European pesticide tax schemes (Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France).

incidental_relevant_studies.title: A Meta-Analysis on the Elasticity of Demand for Pesticides
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Gives the key empirical parameter for a tax (slope of marginal abatement cost via demand elasticity).

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Pathways for advancing pesticide policies
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Policy-mix framework (Möhring et al.).

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Pesticide taxes or voluntary action? An analysis of responses among Norwegian grain farmers
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Farmer response to a doubling of the pesticide price (Norwegian tax).

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Modelling pesticide risk: A marginal cost–benefit analysis of an environmental buffer-zone programme
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Explicit marginal cost-benefit of buffer zones, the third instrument in the Essay 2 ranking.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Financial effect of limiting pesticide use near schools for almonds in nine counties depends on soils and weather
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Economic evaluation of California school-site setbacks, the buffer-zone case the task asked to locate.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Balancing Bees and Pest Management: Projected Costs of Proposed Bee-Protective Neonicotinoid Regulation in California

incidental_relevant_studies.title: The impact of pesticide regulations on suicide in Sri Lanka
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Gunnell et al.: canonical ex post evaluation of HHP bans.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Do Targeted Bans of Insecticides to Prevent Deaths from Self-Poisoning Result in Reduced Agricultural Output?
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Measures the output cost of bans (near zero), an empirical input to the cost of the quantity instrument.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Bans of WHO Class I Pesticides in Bangladesh—suicide prevention without hampering agricultural output
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Ex post effects of bans on both health and agricultural output.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: The cost-effectiveness of banning highly hazardous pesticides to prevent suicides due to pesticide self-ingestion across 14 countries: an economic modelling study
incidental_relevant_studies.why: Economic evaluation of bans as an instrument.

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Impact of paraquat regulation on suicide in South Korea

incidental_relevant_studies.title: Agriculture without paraquat is feasible without loss of productivity—lessons learned from phasing out a highly hazardous herbicide
